messages.subject: Number of fitted values
parts:
Hi,

I recently modeled survival data with INLA. Initially, I have 6,071 observations but when I run the model, I have 34,339 fitted values which are very low compared to my survival data. Because of that, I have issues in order to plot residuals with brinla. Can someone explain why I have so many values ?

Thank you for any insight,
Edwige

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Number of fitted values
parts:
if you use a coxph model, then the poisson extention is used, meaning
that the model is rewritten into poisson regression with more
obversations, see here f.ex

author = {S. Martino and R. Akerkar and H. Rue},
title = {Approximate {B}ayesian Inference for Survival
Models},
journal = SJS,
keywords = {year2010,my.own,my.cv},
year = 2010,
volume = 28,
number = 3,
pages = {514--528}
